key_insight: Power-law photoluminescence decays reveal trap distributions, and a t⁻² decay can occur even when monomolecular—not bimolecular—recombination dominates.
engineering_relevance: More accurate interpretation of photoluminescence transients can guide defect characterization and performance optimization in perovskite solar cells.
method: Analyze experimental photoluminescence transients reported in the literature.
Relate power-law decay exponents to trap distributions.
Examine recombination regimes and limits of differential-lifetime interpretation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports power-law behavior in several published experimental transients but provides no dataset sizes or quantitative fit comparisons.
watch_item: Do not infer the dominant recombination mechanism from a t⁻² decay alone; the abstract describes no AI method.
paper_title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
